title: Storage-neutral dense matrix-vector contract
objective: Define and validate ordinary CPython-parseable one-bulk-operation contracts for dense Matrix times Vector and Vector times Matrix across GF(2), small GF(p), ZZ, and QQ, preserving Sage dimensions, coercion, and result-vector semantics without host scalar boundary loops
references: SageMath 10.9.post2 dense matrix-vector and vector-matrix semantics

oracles: Current Sage.js Matrix and Vector public behavior

handoff.summary: Added an ordinary CPython-parseable storage-neutral contract for dense Matrix times Vector and Vector times Matrix. A validated orientation plan fixes input and output degrees, rejects incompatible dimensions with SageMath's TypeError semantics, and invokes exactly one complete backend operation over opaque matrix/vector storage. Separate row-major scalar fallbacks provide a differential oracle without constructing temporary one-column or one-row matrices. CPython and Sage.js fixtures cover ZZ, QQ, GF(2), and GF(7), explicit mixed-parent widening, incompatible finite fields, exact rational arithmetic, empty shapes, fresh mutable result vectors, invalid storage, one-call execution, and backend failure propagation. The benchmark records public 500 by 500 behavior and the intentionally non-production scalar/materialization fallback at 100 by 100, making the acceleration opportunity measurable.
risks: This lane deliberately does not wire Matrix or Vector, add FFI, or select a physical backend. It defines semantics and a one-bulk-call integration boundary, so it is not itself a public performance improvement.

Current public Sage.js dimension-mismatch multiplication raises ValueError, whereas SageMath 10.9.post2 raises TypeError. Public integration should adopt the contract's TypeError behavior and update the existing public regression expectation.

The callback identity distinguishes right-product from left-product; the side string remains outside the storage ABI. Integration must select the orientation-specific backend operation consistently with the validated plan.
The scalar fallbacks assume entries and zero have already been coerced into the canonical common result parent. Calling them on uncoerced mixed-parent inputs is an integration error.

SageMath has an isolated GF(2) zero-dimensional right-product quirk that returns an immutable zero vector, while other orientations and rings return mutable vectors. This contract intentionally specifies a uniformly fresh mutable result; public integration must retain an explicit regression and document that intentional incompatibility.

The public 500 by 500 benchmark currently takes one warmed sample per orientation to keep the preparation benchmark small, so its raw samples can expose host contention; production performance gates should use the repository's multi-sample normalized methodology.
Only Linux x64 validation ran in this worktree. The new source is pure ordinary Python and JavaScript test code, but the declared platform matrix remains an integration/CI responsibility.
next_steps: Add src/lib/sagejs/linear_algebra/matrix_vector.py to pyrightconfig.json and test/linear-matrix-vector.cjs to the Node test manifest in the integration lane.

Wire Matrix times Vector and Vector times Matrix through canonical Sage parent coercion, prepare one complete storage value for each operand, dispatch exactly one orientation-specific bulk operation, and construct a fresh mutable Vector of plan.result_length.
Implement measured bulk backends for generated FmpzMatrix/FmpqMatrix resources and M4RI/word-prime storage; avoid public temporary matrices and per-entry host boundary calls.
Correct the current public dimension-mismatch exception from ValueError to SageMath-compatible TypeError while preserving distinct-finite-field TypeError behavior.
Add multi-sample public performance gates after the real storage backends land, with result equivalence and construction/coercion costs reported separately.
